There are many other significant emitters in this region that could be served by T-RICH. For example, the Mosaic Company operates a number of phosphate mining and fertilizer production facilities in the region with a combined 627,707 tons of CO 2 emissions according to EPA data. And the City of Tampa operates a waste-to-energy plant just 3.3 miles from the proposed T-RICH site, emitting 120,522 tons of CO in 2023. These and many other emitters in 2 the region can benefit from the T-RICH hub, with options of transporting their captured CO to T-RICH via 2 new pipelines, rail cars or tanker trucks. We analyzed the spatial distribution of significant stationary CO₂ emitters within the Tampa Bay region (central coordinates: 27.9517° N, –82.4588° W) and throughout the state of Florida which involves identifying clusters of high-emission sources such as power plants, industrial facilities, and large manufacturing operations. These sources are typically concentrated near urban centers and along major transportation corridors due to infrastructure availability and proximity to markets.
